name: Upbit
rootCause: South Korean exchange Upbit 342,000 ETH worth about $50 million was stolen. The exchange’s alleged theft occurred while assets were being transferred between hot and cold storage wallets, leading some to speculate that the incident may have been an internal job rather than an external breach. On January 14, 2025, the United States, Japan, and South Korea mentioned in a joint statement that the Upbit theft was attributed to DPRK.

descriptions.text: South Korean exchange Upbit 342,000 ETH worth about $50 million was stolen. The exchange’s alleged theft occurred while assets were being transferred between hot and cold storage wallets, leading some to speculate that the incident may have been an internal job rather than an external breach. On January 14, 2025, the United States, Japan, and South Korea mentioned in a joint statement that the Upbit theft was attributed to DPRK.

On 2019-11-27, attackers transferred 342,000 ETH from an Upbit Ethereum hot wallet to an external address after gaining the ability to authorize withdrawals from the exchange's custody infrastructure. Upbit suspended deposits and withdrawals, moved remaining assets to cold storage, and stated that customer losses would be covered from corporate reserves. Attackers obtained the ability to authorize transfers from Upbit's Ethereum hot wallet infrastructure. Public evidence supports a hot-wallet or signing-system compromise rather than a smart contract vulnerability. The exact intrusion path and method used to obtain signing authority have not been publicly disclosed.
